newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria sell-off in peril - report.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria sell-off in peril - report.

text.p: The privatisation of Bank Austria looked in peril on Sunday when a media report said Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank owned the option to buy the 49 percent voting stake held by Vienna City in Austria's number one bank.
The city's ruling coalition agreed last Tuesday to relinquish its stake in Bank Austria on the condition that the bank remained under Austrian control.
"The privatisation must ensure that a majority Austrian interest remains," the motion said.

But weekly current affairs magazine Profil's Monday edition -- made available in advance -- said the Anteilsverwaltung Zentralsparkasse (AVZ) granted WestLB a buy option for Bank Austria at the end of 1995 when the German bank purchased 10.7 percent of the bank's voting capital.
If WestLB excercises its option to buy AVZ's dossier, it would -- together with its current stake -- hold a significant majority in Bank Austria.

Vienna indirectly controls 45.15 percent of Bank Austria voting stock, or 39.93 percent of share capital, through its AVZ holding. A second firm, Wiener Holding, controls four percent of voting stock, representing 3.53 percent of capital.
Bank Austria spokesman Heimo Hackel confirmed the existence of this hitherto secret agreement between AVZ and WestLB. "Yes it's true -- there is such a contract," Profil quoted him as saying.

In exchange for the Bank Austria buy option, AVZ received the option to buy WestLB's dossier, Profil said. Moreover, WestLB also has the right to dispatch a representative of its choice to Bank Austria's supervisory board.
A process of consultation was also agreed on by the two whereby both would vote the same way at Bank Austria shareholder meetings.
WestLB spokesman Reinhard Parthe told Profil: "We have yet to receive any official information from the AVZ. We have to wait for that and will then decide how we act."

Deputy Vienna mayor Bernhard Goerg of the conservative People's Party has valued AVZ's stake at 25-35 billion schillings, which dwarfs the 17 billion raised for the state in January when Bank Austria bought archrival Creditanstalt.

Vienna foresees a timetable of six years for the privatisation of Bank Austria, whereby buyers for the stake would be sought among institutional investors, strategic partners and via the stock market.
